chapter: The war years: Barnet, Hot Lips Page, Newton and Kirby
title: Joining Lips after Hank Jones; stranded at the Grand Terrace
summary: After sorting out the chronology, he tells how he took Hank Jones's place and was stranded when the Grand Terrace closed, winning over a suspicious bandmate.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Who picked Oscar Pettiford up, Charlie Barnet or Lips?
Oh, wait a minute, now. Charlie Barnet.
Which does come first? Lips Page or Charlie?
Lips Page. Let's go back a minute.
That's right. Oh boy, man, I get diverted.
I mean, how did you come to join Lips in the first place?

Well, his piano player was Hank Jones, and Hank was leaving. So that's how we... I attended a rehearsal sometime, and I joined the band. We went on the road. I remember the first day we played, in South Chicago at the Grand Terrace. The Grand Terrace closed in on us, and we had no money, and then we were stranded in Chicago. There used to be guys that looked at me and they didn't like

the way I looked, because I'd just got back from Europe, you know. These guys were in there, they were right from the South, and they looked like they wanted to do me in, you know. In the first place, I... You know, I just didn't look right to them.
These were guys in Lips' band.

Yeah. So Lips was saying, "Man, you'd better watch these dues." I wouldn't tell you what he really said, but he said words to that effect. He said, "These people are from the South. You're not in Europe now." I said, "No, okay." So I went to this guy and said, "Look, what's your story? Why do you keep on looking at me like this? Do you hate me? What is it? I don't have a dime. I don't know where I'm going to eat." He says, "You don't have a dime? Wait a minute." [LAUGHS] That's all he wanted to know. From then on, I built up stories(?), man; I said, "Look, I'm dead." He brought me a bag of groceries, he brought me money, he brought me everything -- this guy that wanted to...!

Yeah! He thought... I said, "I don't know where I'm going to pay my rent." He said, "Man, I gotta tell you somethin'..." It turned out to be a beautiful friendship. We'd be (?) with the guys playing cards, seeing
